identity.title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Target Stochasticity

problem.claim: Why diffusion and flow-matching methods generalize effectively remains an open question.

gap.claim: The authors address whether the stochastic nature of the conditional flow-matching loss is a key driver of generalization.

contributions.claim: Shows that stochastic and closed-form flow-matching losses are nearly equivalent in high-dimensional settings.
Shows comparable statistical performance for both loss variants in state-of-the-art flow-matching models on standard image datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The work rules out the noisy nature of the flow-matching loss as a key factor driving generalization in flow matching.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report nearly equivalent losses for stochastic and closed-form variants in high-dimensional settings.
The authors report comparable statistical performance on standard image datasets; closed-form training can even improve performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Positions the study within efforts to explain the strong generalization of modern generative models.
Identifies architectural inductive bias and conditional-loss stochasticity as proposed explanations.
Rules out loss noise as a key factor driving flow-matching generalization.
Reports near-equivalent losses and comparable downstream statistical performance, with occasional improvement from the closed-form variant.

source_observation.claim: The abstract tests a proposed explanation by comparing stochastic and closed-form loss variants at both loss and model-performance levels.

lessons.interpretation: A layered comparison can connect a mechanistic hypothesis to observable downstream behavior.
lessons.application: When evaluating a claimed source of generalization, compare the relevant training quantity and end-task performance under a targeted intervention.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when removing the hypothesized factor also changes optimization stability or other confounders that the comparison does not control.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dimensionality, datasets, metrics, model configurations, or statistical tests used.
The reported evidence does not establish that stochasticity is irrelevant in all settings or that the closed-form variant consistently improves performance.
